- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — model tends to over-forecast in bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is trending down, reduce downward bias — model tends to under-forecast in bearish sentiment.
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model often overshoots the peak — cap forecast at 1–2 days after peak.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model tends to over-smooth — increase volatility in forecast near mid-point of horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, especially after 10–15 days, apply downward correction of 3–5% for remaining days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.5), model often fails to anticipate reversal — adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint.
